subject: Re: Partner request - compatibility shim & migration milestones
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@databridgelabs.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Batch endpoint + auth header change request (impact to SDK)

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note from the integrations team at DataBridge Labs — we're planning to consolidate two of our ingestion flows into a single batched inference path. The change includes: 
- a new POST /v2/inference/batch endpoint that accepts a compressed payload format,
- a small change to the auth header (X-DBL-Auth-Version: 2) you'd see on partner calls, and
- removal of the existing stream-compatible query param (?stream=true) on the old endpoint.

We're aware this is potentially breaking for partner SDKs. Can Redwood provide: 
1) a compatibility shim or versioned adapter in your hosted API for a 3-month migration window, and
2) an interim SDK patch so our customers who use the Redwood client libraries don't have to fork their codebases?

Attached is a short design doc (DBL_batch_endpoint_request_v1.pdf) with payload examples and a proposed migration timeline. Our target rollout date is 2027-09-20. Are you able to confirm feasibility and an estimate for the SDK patch?

Thanks — Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Integrations, DataBridge Labs

[Attachment: DBL_batch_endpoint_request_v1.pdf]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@databridgelabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Batch endpoint + auth header change request (impact to SDK)

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the clear doc and timeline. Short answers up front: we can support a compatibility path, but we need to lock a few constraints to keep latency and our SLOs intact. Proposed approach: 

1) Temporary API adapter on Redwood edge: map POST /v2/inference/batch (DBL payload) -> internal /v1/stream-compatible calls for 12 weeks. This reduces partner breakage while we complete SDK changes.
2) SDK patch: we can ship a minor-version SDK (v1.8.1) with a feature flag that accepts DBL payloads and toggles auth header handling.
3) Canary + performance validation: request a dedicated canary window in your staging cluster for two weeks before 2027-09-20.

Open questions from our side: 
- Can you confirm expected average batch sizes and peak concurrency? The adapter's memory profile depends on that.
- Are you planning any retry/ordering guarantees that differ from existing streaming behavior?

I'll loop in our partner-ops and SDK leads to scope effort. If you want, we can draft a mutual action plan with dates and responsibilities by EOD tomorrow.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Batch endpoint + auth header change request — internal scope & ask

Team — forwarding Maya's request (attached). Need quick input so I can confirm timelines with DBL. High-level constraints and proposal: 

Proposal summary (what we tell DBL):
- Provide edge adapter for POST /v2/inference/batch as a stopgap for 12 weeks.
- Ship SDK v1.8.1 with a toggled flag and explicit migration guide.
- Require a 2-week canary run in their staging env + our perf validation.

Questions / asks for tech plan (please reply inline):
- Jonas: memory/cpu impact estimate for adapter if average batch size is 8 requests vs 32. Also need a rough engineering ETA for a prototype shim.
- Vanessa: commercial risk — can we offer the adapter at no extra cost for 3 months as a customer success gesture? Does that affect renewals / credits?
- Marissa: partner comms — we need a short migration guide, deprecation notice, and a sample GitHub PR. Can you take the doc owner?

Risks:
- If we accept unbounded batch sizes, adapter could increase tail latency; need caps or throttling.
- SDK patch introduces extra auth parsing; must be thoroughly tested across languages.

Attachments included: SDK compatibility checklist draft, canary-playbook-steps.md (attached for runbook).

Please respond by EOD so I can give Maya a firm runbook and ETA.

—Stephanie

[Attachment: sdk_compat_shim_proposal.patch]
[Attachment: canary-playbook-steps.md]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@databridgelabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T16:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Batch endpoint + auth header change request (mutual action plan)

Maya —

Thanks for the patience. Internal alignment complete; summary and next steps below (also attaching the proposed SDK patch and canary steps).

Mutual action plan: 
- 2027-08-04: Redwood creates edge adapter prototype and opens GH PR (redwood-sdk #847). Owner: Jonas.
- 2027-08-10: Redwood publishes SDK v1.8.1 beta with feature-flag support for X-DBL-Auth-Version. Owner: Marissa.
- 2027-08-15 through 2027-08-29: Two-week canary in DBL staging. Redwood will run perf validation and report token-latency percentiles daily. Owner: Vanessa + Partner CS.
- 2027-09-20: Target GA for DBL rollout. After GA we will deprecate the old ?stream=true behavior with a 12-week notice to customers; final removal date = 2027-12-13.

Engineering notes/limits: 
- We will cap batch size at 64 items for the adapter; larger payloads will return 413 with migration guidance.
- Edge adapter will not change model routing — model version pinning still applies.

Deliverables attached: sdk_compat_shim_proposal.patch, canary-playbook-steps.md. Please confirm acceptance of the plan and that the proposed dates work on your side. If agreed, we'll spin up the staging slot and share GH PRs.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
